source:
Sofia: I know the ICU buffer matters, but clearing the delayed cancer surgery backlog should get priority for the next two weeks. Every postponed case means another family waiting for a biopsy or tumor removal.
Malik: I know the backlog matters, but keep eight ICU beds empty through flu season. If a respiratory surge arrives, cancelled surgeries are bad; no ICU bed for an emergency is worse.
Sofia: We can reserve four beds and still move the longest-delayed cases.
Malik: Four beds is not enough margin when staffing is already thin.

extraction.mainQuestion: Should the hospital prioritize clearing delayed cancer surgeries or preserving a larger ICU buffer?

positions.label: Prioritize delayed surgeries
positions.thesis: The hospital should prioritize clearing delayed cancer surgeries over keeping the full ICU buffer for the next two weeks.
positions.steelman: Long-delayed cancer cases are urgent enough to justify using some ICU margin while preserving a smaller reserve.

groundingQuotes.quote: clearing the delayed cancer surgery backlog should get priority for the next two weeks.

positions.label: Preserve ICU buffer
positions.thesis: The hospital should keep eight ICU beds empty through flu season even if surgeries remain delayed.
positions.steelman: A respiratory surge could make ICU capacity more urgent than reducing the surgery backlog right now.

groundingQuotes.quote: keep eight ICU beds empty through flu season.

claims.statement: Delayed cancer surgeries should take priority over preserving the full ICU buffer for two weeks.

resolution.condition: The hospital must decide how to weight delayed cancer care against surge capacity.

groundingQuotes.quote: Every postponed case means another family waiting for a biopsy or tumor removal.

claims.statement: A larger ICU buffer should take priority because a respiratory surge could make emergency capacity scarce.

resolution.condition: The hospital must decide how much ICU margin to preserve under flu-season uncertainty.
